_about: Fixed briefs, one per pipeline path. Never edit a brief after a baseline has been recorded against it: add a new id instead, or the comparison silently measures two different tasks.
_preset: The skill is interactive. Headless runs cannot answer it, so every CONFIG parameter is given up front and the session is told to proceed in auto mode. This is a deviation from canonical use, recorded in bench/README.md.

briefs.prompt: /kiln A hanging iron lantern with a glass cage and a ring on top, for a medieval inn. Type: prop. Style: stylized. Export: glTF. Detail tier: balanced. Mode: auto. Storage: compact. Create it by scripted modeling in Blender — no marketplace, no AI generation.

/kiln A cluster of three stylized fantasy mushrooms with spotted caps, for a forest scene. Type: prop. Style: stylized. Export: glTF. Detail tier: balanced. Mode: auto. Storage: compact. 3D backend: hf-spaces. Create it by AI generation.

/kiln A realistic wooden chair for a farmhouse kitchen. Type: prop. Style: realistic. Export: glTF. Detail tier: balanced. Mode: auto. Storage: compact. Source it from PolyHaven — no AI generation, no Sketchfab.

/kiln A sci-fi supply crate with reinforced corners and a handle on each side. Type: prop. Style: realistic. Export: glTF. Detail tier: balanced. Mode: auto. Storage: compact. Model it by script, then texture it with PolyHaven PBR textures.

/kiln A low-poly humanoid villager, rigged and ready for animation in a web game. Type: character. Style: low-poly. Export: glTF. Detail tier: lightweight. Mode: auto. Storage: compact. Create it by scripted modeling, then rig it.

/kiln batch Scene: a blacksmith's workshop. Assets: a wooden stool, a water bucket, a coiled rope. Style: stylized. Palette: warm browns and iron grey. Export: glTF. Detail tier: lightweight. Storage: compact. Creation method: scripted modeling for all three. Then run the batch with /kiln batch run --all.

briefs.path: 3D print: a box with a bayonet lid
briefs.prompt: /kiln A small round box with a bayonet lid — push down and twist to lock — to 3D-print, about 60 mm across. Type: prop. Style: stylized. Print: FDM, 0.4 mm nozzle, one colour; the box and the lid as two separate STL files. Export: STL. Mode: auto. Storage: compact. Create it by scripted modeling. Standing answer, given in advance because nobody can answer during this run: if you would send a mechanical part to a CAD tool, carry on anyway — the user accepts a lid made to decorative precision and will print any test piece you write first.

briefs.path: Kiln Studio: a note pinned in the page, handled by Studio's own Claude worker

studio.note: The top ring is too small to hang it: make it twice as big, still attached to the roof.

record: the ring's scale against the 2x asked (median of its three bounds)
the ring still touching the roof
the note answered and marked addressed, a new version exported
approvals the worker asked for (free allowed, paid denied) and proposals answered
the page's screenshots, before and after (shots/)
briefs.prompt: (Studio) The top ring is too small to hang it: make it twice as big, still attached to the roof.

_answers: A headless session cannot answer a question: one it asks ends the run. A brief that must get past a proposal says its answer up front, as a standing answer in the prompt, word for word the same for every version measured (ref-ammo-box-project). The original brief stays as it was, so it records whether the skill proposes when nobody has answered (ref-ammo-box), and ref-lantern is the negative control: a photo with no markings, where nothing should be proposed.
_fields: inputs: files under runs/_refs measured before the session, to compare with what it ships. finals: the shipped-file patterns (default *_final.glb). print: {process, assembly} runs the bench's print_check on the shipped STL/3MF. disabled: the reason a brief is not run. studio: a brief run through Kiln Studio (studio_drive.py) — fixture under bench/fixtures, the note pinned on object, what its change must measure; prompt is then only the note, for reading.
